subject: Mutual plan kickoff — Dedicated GPU pool for RetailAI (throughput SLOs & eval cadence)
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena@retailai.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Torres <sam.torres@retailai.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated GPU pool — kickoff & initial throughput targets

Hi Irene / Marissa,

Thanks for the intro. RetailAI is ready to kick off a mutual action plan to evaluate Redwood Dedicated for our recommendation engine pipelines. High-level asks up front so we can align the MAP:

- Target production throughput: ~10k tokens/sec sustained per cluster (peak bursts to 18k) across two primary endpoints (re-ranking + contextual search).
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 150ms for 1k-token requests, p50 << 80ms.
- Pilot scope: 6-week evaluation, 2-week canary followed by a 4-week load ramp.
- Compliance: SOC2 evidence and basic network topology questions (we can share our security contact).

Attached is a small spreadsheet with estimated daily traffic by endpoint and preferred pilot start windows. Can we schedule a 45-minute kickoff this week to agree roles, deliverables, and a short evaluation plan?

I'll loop procurement (procurement@retailai.com) once we have a draft MAP and timelines.

Thanks — Elena

--
Elena Park
Head of ML Platform | RetailAI Inc.
Attachments: RetailAI_expected_traffic_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 38KB)

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@retailai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU pool — kickoff & initial throughput targets

Elena — great to meet you (virtually). Welcome and thanks for the clear initial targets. Proposed next steps from Redwood to get the MAP moving:

1) Shared MAP template (attached) — we will pre-fill Roles & Deliverables before the kickoff.
2) Technical intake — Marissa will work with your SREs to get trace/sample payloads and sequence-length distributions.
3) Evaluation plan — 2-week canary (small dedicated pool), then 4-week customer validation with progressive traffic ramps.
4) Procurement checklist — simple contract addendum for Dedicated capacity; we can sync with procurement@retailai.com once scope is locked.

Proposed kickoff: Thu 16 Sep, 10:00–10:45 PT. If that works, we will send a calendar invite with pre-reads (MAP template + test-playbook).

I have CC'd Karthik (billing/commit sizing) and Dylan (serving runtime lead) to cover capacity and performance validation.

Irene Choi
Senior Account Director | Redwood Inference

On Wed, Sep 15, 2026 at 09:18 AM Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com> wrote:
> Proposed kickoff: Thu 16 Sep, 10:00–10:45 PT.

Quick tech checklist from my side to make the 1st session productive: please share (or confirm) the following before the kickoff if possible:
- Representative request/response sizes and sequence-length distribution (we need the 50th, 95th percentiles).
- Expected concurrency per endpoint and any burst patterns (hourly/daily peaks).
- Any hard constraints on model variants (quantized vs fp16), and whether you need deterministic outputs for evals.
- A short list of 3–5 critical prompts for quality checks (we'll use these in the eval cadence).

I'll bring a small benchmark harness and a suggested throughput-first configuration (initial batch sizes, KV cache suggestions). I'll also upload a brief technical pre-read to the shared drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0B_retailai/onboarding/pilot-sheet

Thanks — Thu 16 Sep 10:00 PT works. I've attached a slightly expanded traffic sheet with endpoint mappings and retention notes. A couple clarifications before we meet:

- The 10k tokens/sec is an aggregate across two clusters; can you confirm whether Redwood examples are per-cluster or per-pool?
- For the canary, we'd like one cluster (3 x A100 equivalent) reserved and a rollback plan if p95 exceeds 200ms under synthetic load.
- Procurement will want a 30-day pilot agreement; I added procurement@retailai.com to the thread.
